drivingQuestion: Does the mishna prove that an agent who adds to his agency remains an agent?
outcomeNote: The inference from the mishna is deflected by Rav Sheshet's oqimta.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: דְּאָמַר שָׁלִיחַ: טוֹל אַחַת מִדַּעְתּוֹ וְאַחַת מִדַּעְתִּי.
segments.en: «Rav Sheshet said» that this inference is not necessarily correct, because the mishna can be explained as referring specifically to a case «where» the «agent said» to the guests: «Take one» piece of meat «in accordance with the intent» of the homeowner «and one» piece «in accordance with my intent.»

segments.he: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: עָקַר שָׁלִיחַ שְׁלִיחוּתֵיהּ דְּבַעַל הַבַּיִת, וְלָא לִמְעוֹל – קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: Rav Sheshet adds that it is necessary for the mishna to teach this halakha, «lest you say» that the «agent has uprooted the agency of the homeowner» by adding to his instructions, «and» therefore the homeowner is «not» liable for the prohibition of «misuse» even for the first piece of meat. Consequently, the mishna «teaches us» that the homeowner is also liable.

moves.summary: the case is where the agent separated the pieces explicitly
moves.about: the mishna does not prove that an adding agent remains an agent

moves.summary: one might think the agent uprooted the owner's agency
moves.about: the novelty: the agent's addition does not uproot the owner's agency

moves.summary: the mishna teaches the owner is still liable

edges.about: the mishna does not prove that an adding agent remains an agent

edges.about: the agent explicitly separated the owner's piece from his own
the novelty: the agent's addition does not uproot the owner's agency

positions.claim: the mishna speaks of an agent who said: one by his intent and one by mine
